digest.intro: AI cracks 27-year-old math, robots go to the border, Rome made nanoglass.

items.title: Israel votes — first election since October 7
items.blurb: Israelis are at the polls today for the first time in nearly four years, with 22,000 police deployed and no bloc currently holding a majority — Netanyahu vs. Eisenkot, both right, with entirely different theories of the post-war order. Meanwhile the whole regional architecture is in motion: Qatar is brokering a five-day Hormuz-for-naval-blockade trade, Pezeshkian is in Moscow meeting Putin, and the Houthis just branded Egypt's Saudi deployment a declaration of war.

items.title: Section 702 renewal push — while a damaging FISA court ruling stays buried
items.blurb: Seven months ago the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court found that intelligence analysts were pulling Americans' messages without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires — and approved another year of surveillance anyway. That ruling was supposed to be publicly released by September 13; it still hasn't been, and the administration is now pressing Congress to reauthorize Section 702 before the ruling surfaces. Senators Wyden and Schiff are calling it illegal withholding; the program itself lapsed in June but collection continues under the court's March approval.

items.title: Boston Dynamics employees petition to block robot dog sale to ICE — executives say no
items.blurb: More than 300 Boston Dynamics employees signed a petition — half anonymous — asking executives to cancel a $1.3M DHS contract sending modified Spot robots to ICE, after friends and family started asking them 'how can you live with yourselves.' Executives declined, promising the robots won't be weaponized, which is a promise with no enforcement mechanism. This is the dual-use dilemma made visceral: the people who built the thing can't stop what it becomes.

items.title: OpenAI says AI disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis — here's what was actually proven
items.blurb: Three simultaneous claims: AI-generated proofs that (1) disprove the 27-year-old ETH — meaning the belief that scheduling, routing, and chip-layout problems have no fundamental shortcut around brute-force search may be wrong; (2) prove the local smoothing conjecture in all dimensions at once, where humans had only cracked it dimension-by-dimension, with the 3D case as recently as this year; and (3) partially advance the Yang-Mills existence proof underlying the strong nuclear force. All three are Lean-verified and sent to external experts including Nobel laureate David Gross. This explainer is the right place to start before hitting the preprint.

items.title: Will the real Anthropic please stand up
items.blurb: Anthropic filed its IPO prospectus the same week a federal judge ruled it trained Claude on illegally obtained books — a $1.5B settlement covering nearly 500,000 works — and the 335-page filing simultaneously warns that its technology could 'pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity' while asking investors to see their purchase as 'an opportunity to be part of something greater.' MIT Tech Review reads this as a decade of masterful narrative capture meeting its first stress test. The structural contradiction between safety-lab identity and public-market logic is now legally documented.

items.title: Genie 4: DeepMind's world-model generates interactive 3D environments in real time
items.blurb: Text or image prompt in, fully interactive navigable 3D world out — with simultaneous audio, ambient sound, and dialogue generated in real time using keyboard controls. Genie 4 builds on Gemini Omni for visual grounding and separate Gemini models for coherence and continuity, designed as much for robot training environments as for interactive experiences. For someone working in WebGL and generative 3D, this is the substrate question getting very loud very fast.

items.title: Roman nanotechnology, rebuilt: The Lycurgus Cup's recipe cracked and cast as new sculpture
items.blurb: The Lycurgus Cup — made around 400 CE — glows green in reflected light and blood-red in transmitted light because Roman artisans accidentally suspended gold-silver nanoparticles in the glass when they added salt during melting, causing the electrons to vibrate differently depending on the observer's vantage point. University of Sheffield scientists finally cracked the exact recipe and rebuilt it as a contemporary sculpture with the same dichroic effect. It's the same phenomenon as daguerreotype color shifts and photonic crystal iridescence — ancient and modern nanotechnology arriving at the same optical trick from opposite directions.

items.title: Izumi Kato: Totemic figures at Perrotin New York — opens today
items.blurb: Kato's hitogata figures — part infant, part ancient, eyes swirling like pools — open today at Perrotin in a show where flat canvas and cast aluminum stones suspended from the ceiling play the same perceptual game as the Lycurgus Cup: meaning shifts with how you look. His wooden sculptures are painted with exactly the same approach as his canvases, collapsing the distinction between flat and volumetric. Worth the walk.

facts.fact: The FISA court ruling finding illegal warrantless searches of Americans' communications was supposed to be publicly released by September 13, 2026 — it still hasn't been, past the administration's own statutory deadline.
The Anthropic copyright settlement — $1.5 billion covering nearly 500,000 registered works — is described by the Authors Alliance as the largest copyright settlement involving an AI company.

Since June 2026, organized thieves using GPS spoofing and hijacked freight-broker accounts have stolen more than $100 million in data-center-bound cargo — servers, fiber-optic cables, memory chips, and bitcoin mining machines — from US highways.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film that works like a system — memory, image, time, and technology interlocked into something that feels less like a documentary and more like a piece of generative software for the brain. If you love the edge where technology reshapes how humans construct reality, this is the source text.

art_picks.title: Blind Time Drawings
art_picks.creator: Robert Morris
art_picks.why: Morris made these with his eyes shut, recording duration and pressure rather than mark — the body as input device, the drawing as a readout of a process you can't see. It's the conceptual ancestor of everything from generative WebGL to biometric art, and it still hits harder than most of its descendants.

art_picks.title: Selected Ambient Works Volume II
art_picks.creator: Aphex Twin
art_picks.why: Fifty-four pieces built almost entirely from texture and environmental drift — it functions less as music you listen to and more as a system you inhabit. The album's total lack of titles (originally) and refusal of narrative structure makes it feel like a generative environment rather than a composition.

events.name: Pierre Huyghe: UUmwelt
events.venue: MoMA Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden, Manhattan
events.why: Freestanding screens across MoMA's outdoor sculpture garden show hallucinatory images generated by a neural network trained on fMRI brain scans — your gaze and movement, detected by sensors, influence which images appear and in what sequence, making you a live variable in a system that tries to reconstruct thought.

events.name: Haegue Yang: Through
events.why: Yang's largest US commission fills both levels of Dia Beacon with a new body of work structured by Five Phases cosmology and a decade-long posthumous collaboration with exiled Korean composer Isang Yun — it's a translation system, turning music, philosophy, and political history into spatial and chromatic form across an industrial minimalist building.

events.name: Oliver Bak — Solo Exhibition
events.why: The young Danish painter's New York debut at Sprüth Magers: figures and flora submerged in translucent veils, art-historically loaded but temporally unmoored — Bak's paintings feel like they're emerging from and dissolving back into their own surfaces simultaneously, the kind of craft obsession that makes you want to go make something.

events.name: Playback: The Brooklyn Watch Party
events.why: Spike Lee, BAM, and NY Liberty owner Clara Wu Tsai co-produced a two-day festival of repertory film, live performances, and a free street fair — it's a deliberate attempt to build communal ritual around film and Brooklyn cultural identity, which is worth watching as an experiment in what happens when institutions try to re-create a scene.

events.name: Boutique Design New York (BDNY) 2026
events.why: A hospitality and spatial design fair with 700+ brands including 100 first-timers, organized around immersive installations and material environments — less trade show, more a compressed survey of where sensory design is heading, useful if you're watching how physical space gets designed as an experience system.
